records.title: Statin initiation and cognitive function in older adults: a randomised double-blind trial
records.abstract: Background: Whether statin initiation affects cognition in older adults remains debated. In this randomised, double-blind trial, 48 older adults with mild subjective memory complaints were randomised to atorvastatin 40 mg or placebo for 12 months. The primary outcome was change in digit span. At 12 months, statin initiation showed SMD 0.62 (95% CI 0.21 to 1.03) in favour of statin initiation on working memory. Adverse events were balanced between groups.

records.title: Effects of lipid-lowering therapy on ADAS-Cog scores: a double-blind randomised controlled trial
records.abstract: Aim: To test lipid-lowering therapy in older adults. We conducted a double-blind randomised controlled trial in which 120 participants aged 65-80 received rosuvastatin 20 mg or placebo. Cognition was assessed with ADAS-Cog at baseline and 24 months. At 24 months the adjusted mean difference -1.8 points (95% CI -3.1 to -0.5) on the ADAS-Cog favoured statin therapy (lower scores indicate better performance). Retention was 94%.

records.title: Statin use and incident cognitive decline: a prospective cohort study
records.abstract: We followed a prospective cohort study of 2,140 community-dwelling adults aged 70 and above for three annual waves. Statin initiators were compared with non-users using propensity-score weighting. Over 36 months, initiators had adjusted hazard ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.99) for incident cognitive decline on the 3MS scale. Residual confounding cannot be excluded.

records.title: Simvastatin and memory performance: a placebo-controlled cross-over trial
records.abstract: We ran a placebo-controlled cross-over trial with two 10-week periods. 24 older adults with normal baseline cognition received simvastatin 40 mg or placebo in random order. Verbal recall showed SMD 0.31 (95% CI -0.12 to 0.74) favouring statin, not reaching conventional significance. Washout was four weeks.

records.title: Cognitive outcomes after statin switching: a retrospective chart review
records.abstract: This retrospective chart review examined 63 inpatients switched to a different statin. Cognitive screening used an unvalidated bedside checklist. Switching was associated with OR 1.42 (95% CI 0.58 to 3.47) for reported confusion. No adjustment for delirium history was possible.

records.title: Statins and the brain: a narrative review of mechanisms
records.abstract: This narrative review summarises proposed mechanisms linking statins to cognition, without systematic search or pooled effect estimates.

records.title: Statin therapy and working memory in healthy young volunteers
records.abstract: We recruited university students aged 18-25 for a single-dose crossover experiment measuring reaction time. Older adults were not studied.
